# Enterprise Architecture Platform Automation

**← Back to [EAP Home](../README.md)**

---

> This document provides an overview of the automated workflows and publishing processes for the Enterprise Architecture Platform, including documentation publishing using AWS EKS containerized deployment and comprehensive change detection with email notifications.
page_texts.2:
[.github/README.md#architecture-overview]

## Architecture Overview

The repository uses a modern containerized automation architecture supporting enterprise-grade documentation deployment:

- **📄 Scripts** (`scripts/`) - Python processing scripts for content analysis, deployment, and notifications
- **🔄 Workflows** (`workflows/`) - GitHub Actions workflows for AWS EKS deployment with environment isolation
- **📧 Templates** (`templates/`) - HTML and email templates for professional stakeholder communication
- **👥 CODEOWNERS** - Code ownership and review requirements for architecture domains
- **🚀 EKS Deployment** - Containerized MKDocs platform with Kubernetes orchestration
- **🔒 Environment Isolation** - Separate dev and prod environments with dedicated configurations
page_texts.3:
[.github/README.md#production-scripts]

### Production Scripts

The `scripts/` directory contains production-ready scripts organized by function:
page_texts.4:
[.github/README.md#processing-scripts]

#### **Processing Scripts**

- **`content_change_analyzer.py`**: Platform-agnostic content change detection and analysis
- **`status_dashboard.py`**: Generic deployment status tracking and progress monitoring
- **`identify_files_to_index.py`**: Intelligent file identification comparing sitemap against OpenSearch state for incremental indexing
- **`create_rag_content_payload.py`**: RAG content payload creation from filtered file list
page_texts.5:
[.github/README.md#notification-scripts]

#### **Notification Scripts**

- **`detailed.py`**: Comprehensive success notifications with deployment details and change summaries
- **`failure.py`**: Detailed failure notifications with diagnostic information
- **`template_utils.py`**: Email templating, content categorization, and notification utilities
- **`test_smtp.py`**: SMTP connectivity testing and configuration validation

All scripts are designed to work with containerized deployments and support both EKS and future deployment platforms.

### Modern Templates

The `templates/` directory provides comprehensive templating:

- **Container-Ready HTML**: Modern, responsive HTML conversion optimized for containerized deployments
- **Email Notifications**: Professional HTML templates with deployment links, file categorization, and change detection
- **Platform-Agnostic**: Templates designed to work with EKS and future container orchestration platforms

### 📚 Documentation Platform

- **MKDocs Platform** - Static site generation with containerization support
- **AWS EKS Publishing** - Kubernetes container orchestration with high availability

[.github/README.md#-rag-service-platform]

### 🤖 RAG Service Platform

- **RAG Service** - Retrieval-Augmented Generation service for AI-powered documentation search
- **OpenSearch Integration** - AWS OpenSearch for vector embeddings and semantic search (via VPC endpoints)
- **Bedrock Integration** - AWS Bedrock for LLM models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) and embeddings (Titan) via VPC endpoints
- **Shared Ingress** - NGINX Ingress Controller routes paths: `/api/v1/*` → RAG service, `/` → documentation
- **Intelligent Indexing** - Kubernetes Job with VPC access queries OpenSearch to skip unchanged files (~80-90% reduction)
- **Service Account** - IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) for secure, credential-free AWS service access

## Key Features

- ✅ **🆕 Environment-Based Deployment** - Dedicated dev and prod environments with isolated configurations
- ✅ **🆕 GitHub Environment Integration** - Environment-specific variables and secrets management
- ✅ **🆕 Kubernetes Container Orchestration** - High-availability deployment with multi-pod architecture
- ✅ **🆕 AWS EKS Integration** - Enterprise-grade container orchestration platform
- ✅ **🆕 Ingress Management** - NGINX Ingress Controller with Network Load Balancer and custom domain support
- ✅ **🆕 Container Registry Integration** - AWS ECR for secure Docker image management
- ✅ **🆕 RAG Service Integration** - AI-powered documentation search with vector embeddings and LLM integration
- ✅ **🆕 OpenSearch Vector Store** - Semantic search capabilities with automatic content indexing
- ✅ **🆕 Shared Ingress Architecture** - RAG-owned Ingress with path-based routing for all services
- ✅ **⚡ Intelligent Incremental Indexing** - Kubernetes Job with VPC access queries OpenSearch to skip unchanged files (~80-90% reduction)
- ✅ **🎯 Smart File Identification** - Dual-path matching (leaf vs directory), URL decoding, size/mtime comparison
- ✅ **🔄 Automatic PR Merge Deployment** - Zero-friction documentation updates on main branch merges to dev environment
- ✅ **🔄 Smart Path Filtering** - Only deploys when documentation content actually changes
- ✅ **🔄 Enhanced Change Detection** - Integrated content analysis for meaningful deployment notifications
- ✅ **🔄 Manual Environment Selection** - Choose dev or prod environment for manual deployments
- ✅ **🔄 Automated RAG Indexing** - Content changes trigger automatic embedding updates via API integration
- ✅ **🔒 OIDC Authentication** - No static AWS credentials, uses secure token exchange for temporary credentials
- ✅ **🔒 Environment Isolation** - Separate AWS IAM roles and configurations per environment
- ✅ **🤖 Intelligent Content Analysis** - Platform-agnostic change detection and deployment optimization
- ✅ **📧 Professional Notifications** - Environment-aware email alerts with deployment details and change summaries
- ✅ **⚙️ Flexible Deployment Modes** - Full sync, changed-only, and section-specific deployment options
- ✅ **🎯 Target Section Deployment** - Deploy specific architectural domains for focused updates
- ✅ **📋 Asset Management** - Automated deployment of images, CSS, and brand assets with containerization
- ✅ **🌐 Custom Domain Support** - Environment-specific ingress configuration with SSL termination
- ✅ **🚀 Modern Container Architecture** - Docker-based builds with Kubernetes deployment automation

## Workflow Triggers

The repository supports environment-aware automatic and manual deployment workflows:

- **🤖 Automatic Deployment** (`deploy-mkdocs-platform.yml`):
    - **Trigger**: Pull request merge to main branch (documentation changes only)
    - **Target Environment**: Always deploys to **dev environment**
    - **Smart Filtering**: Only triggers when documentation files are modified
    - **Configuration**: Optimized defaults for development testing
    - **Platform**: AWS EKS with containerized MKDocs deployment
    - **Sync Mode**: changed-only for optimal performance
    - **Intelligent Indexing**: Kubernetes Job filters unchanged files (~80-90% reduction in indexing)
    - **API Integration**: Calls RAG service `/api/rag/v1/index` endpoint with filtered content
    - **Notifications**: Enabled for stakeholder communication with change detection
    - **Namespace**: `eapref-app` (shared namespace)
    - **Domain**: Uses dev ingress configuration
    - **Zero Friction**: No manual intervention required after PR approval

- **👤 Manual Deployment** (`deploy-mkdocs-platform.yml`):
    - **Trigger**: Manual workflow dispatch with full environment control
    - **Environment Selection**: Choose **dev** or **prod** environment from dropdown
    - **Platform**: AWS EKS with Kubernetes container orchestration
    - **Sync Options**: changed-only, section-specific, or full-sync modes
    - **Target Sections**: Deploy all sections or specific documentation areas
    - **Intelligent Indexing**: Optional file filtering for incremental indexing
    - **API Integration**: Indexes content via RAG service endpoints
    - **Environment Variables**: Automatically uses environment-specific configurations
    - **Namespace**: `eapref-app` (shared across environments)
    - **Domain**: Environment-specific ingress hosts (dev vs prod)
    - **Asset Control**: Choose whether to include/exclude asset files
    - **Notifications**: Enable/disable email notifications as needed

- **🤖 RAG Service Deployment** (`deploy-rag-service.yml`):
    - **Trigger**: Manual workflow dispatch or pull request merge with RAG service changes
    - **Environment Selection**: Choose **dev** or **prod** environment
    - **Platform**: AWS EKS with shared Ingress management
    - **Ingress Ownership**: Creates authoritative shared Ingress with all service paths
    - **Path Routing**: Complete configuration: `/api/v1/*` → RAG, `/` → MkDocs
    - **OpenSearch Integration**: Vector storage with AWS OpenSearch Service (VPC endpoints)
    - **Bedrock Models**: Claude 3.5 Sonnet for LLM, Titan for embeddings (VPC endpoints)
    - **IRSA**: Service account with IAM roles for credential-free AWS access
    - **API Endpoints**: `/api/rag/v1/index`, `/api/rag/v1/search`, `/api/rag/v1/stats`
    - **Prerequisites**: Requires RAG infrastructure deployment (OpenSearch, security groups)
    - **Namespace**: `eapref-app` (shared with MkDocs)

- **🔍 Automated Verification** (`verify-mkdocs-platform.yml`):
    - **Trigger**: Push to any branch, pull requests to main
    - **Scope**: MKDocs platform component validation and container build testing
    - **Purpose**: Quality assurance and continuous integration
    - **No Deployment**: Validates content and configuration without deploying to environments

[.github/README.md#environment-configuration]

### Environment Configuration

- **Dev Environment**:
    - **Namespace**: `eapref-app` (shared with prod)
    - **Ingress Host**: Environment-specific domain (configurable)
    - **Purpose**: Development testing and automatic PR merge deployments
    - **AWS Authentication**: OIDC with dev IAM role

- **Prod Environment**:
    - **Namespace**: `eapref-app` (shared with dev)
    - **Ingress Host**: Environment-specific domain (configurable)
    - **Purpose**: Production deployments (manual only)
    - **AWS Authentication**: OIDC with production IAM role

- **Shared Namespace Benefits**:
    - **Simplified Management**: Single namespace for both environments
    - **Resource Sharing**: Shared NGINX Ingress Controller
    - **Path-Based Routing**: Environment differentiation via ingress host, not namespace
    - **Cost Efficiency**: Reduced cluster resource overhead
page_texts.15:
[.github/README.md#deployment-architecture]

### Deployment Architecture

- **Container Platform**: AWS EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service)
- **Container Registry**: AWS ECR (Elastic Container Registry)
- **Service Architecture**: Kubernetes ClusterIP with NGINX Ingress Controller behind Network Load Balancer
- **High Availability**: Multi-pod deployment with load balancing
- **Resource Management**: CPU and memory limits with auto-scaling capabilities
- **Authentication**: OIDC (OpenID Connect) for secure, credential-free AWS access
- **RAG Integration**: API-based content indexing with intelligent filtering (~80-90% reduction)

**Note**: All deployments include environment-aware email notifications with fully qualified URLs to deployed content.

[.github/README.md#environment-specific-variables-per-environment]

### Environment-Specific Variables (Per Environment)

Configure these variables in **each environment** (dev and prod):

| Variable Name | Description | Example Value (Dev) | Example Value (Prod) |
|---------------|-------------|---------------------|----------------------|
| `AWS_IAM_ROLE` | AWS IAM role ARN for OIDC authentication | `arn:aws:iam::707203271462:role/github-actions-dev` | `arn:aws:iam::703319747816:role/github-actions-prod` |
| `ECR_REGISTRY_URL` | AWS ECR registry URL | `707203271462.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` | `703319747816.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` |
| `ECR_REPOSITORY_NAME` | ECR repository name | `pfe-pg-dev-us1-cm-ecr-platform-shared` | `pfe-pg-prd-us1-cm-ecr-platform-shared` |
| `EKS_CLUSTER_NAME` | EKS cluster name | `pfe-pg-dev-us1-cm-eks-shared` | `pfe-pg-prd-us1-cm-eks-shared` |
| `EKS_INGRESS_HOST` | Environment-specific domain | `eap-reference-dev.example.com` | `eap-reference.example.com` |
| `OPENSEARCH_URL` | OpenSearch domain endpoint (RAG only) | `vpc-dev-us1-cm-osd-...` | `vpc-prd-us1-cm-osd-...` |
| `OPENSEARCH_INDEX_NAME` | OpenSearch index name (RAG only) | `ea-documentation-dev` | `ea-documentation-prod` |
| `SMTP_SERVER` | Environment-specific SMTP server | `smtp-dev.company.com` | `smtp.company.com` |
page_texts.19:
[.github/README.md#environment-specific-secrets-per-environment]

### Environment-Specific Secrets (Per Environment)

**No AWS credentials required!** The workflows use **OIDC (OpenID Connect)** authentication instead of static AWS credentials.

**Optional SMTP Authentication (Per Environment):**

| Secret Name | Description | Required |
|-------------|-------------|----------|
| `SMTP_USERNAME` | Email username for notifications | Optional (only if SMTP requires auth) |
| `SMTP_PASSWORD` | Email password for notifications | Optional (only if SMTP requires auth) |
| `RAG_API_KEY` | RAG service API key (if enabled) | Optional (for RAG indexing) |

**OIDC Authentication Benefits:**

- ✅ No long-lived AWS access keys stored in GitHub
- ✅ Temporary credentials via secure token exchange
- ✅ GitHub Actions assumes IAM roles directly using short-lived tokens
- ✅ Automatic credential rotation
- ✅ Enhanced security posture
page_texts.20:
[.github/README.md#repository-variables-global]

### Repository Variables (Global)

Configure these variables at the repository level (shared across environments):

| Variable Name | Description | Default Value |
|---------------|-------------|---------------|
| `NOTIFICATION_EMAILS` | Email addresses for notifications | (comma-separated list) |
| `SMTP_PORT` | SMTP server port | `587` |
| `SMTP_SUBJECT` | Email subject prefix | `[EAP Docs]` |
| `SMTP_FROM_EMAIL` | From email address | (your notification email) |
page_texts.21:
[.github/README.md#aws-iam-requirements]

### AWS IAM Requirements

Each environment requires AWS IAM permissions via **OIDC-enabled IAM roles**:

**Prerequisites for OIDC:**

1. Configure GitHub as an OIDC provider in AWS IAM
2. Create IAM role with trust policy allowing GitHub Actions from this repository
3. Set `AWS_IAM_ROLE` variable (documented above) pointing to the role ARN
4. Workflow includes `id-token: write` permission (already configured in workflows)

**IAM Role Permissions Required:**

- **EKS**: Cluster access and kubectl configuration (`eks:DescribeCluster`, `eks:ListClusters`)
- **ECR**: Container registry access for image push/pull (`ecr:*`)
- **Route 53**: DNS management for custom domains (if applicable)
- **Network Load Balancer**: Ingress controller permissions (if using NLB)

**RAG Service Additional IAM Requirements:**

For RAG service deployment, additional permissions are required:

- **OpenSearch**: Full access to the OpenSearch Service cluster via IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts)
- **Bedrock**: Access to Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Titan embedding models via VPC endpoints
- **IAM**: Permissions to assume the RAG service role via IRSA
- **S3**: Access to any S3 buckets containing content to be indexed (if applicable)

**IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts):**

The RAG service uses IRSA for credential-free access to AWS services from within Kubernetes pods. The `rag-service-account` Kubernetes service account is annotated with the IAM role ARN, allowing pods to assume the role automatically.
page_texts.22:
[.github/README.md#workflow-configuration]

### Workflow Configuration

The workflows automatically:

1. **Environment Selection**: Uses the selected environment's variables and secrets
2. **OIDC Authentication**: Assumes IAM role using GitHub's OIDC provider for temporary credentials
3. **Namespace Management**: Deploys to the shared `eapref-app` namespace (used by both dev and prod)
4. **Domain Management**: Routes traffic to environment-specific domains via shared Ingress
5. **Container Orchestration**: Manages EKS deployments with proper resource allocation
6. **Intelligent Indexing**: Kubernetes Job queries OpenSearch to identify only changed files
page_texts.23:
[.github/README.md#setup-steps]

### Setup Steps

1. **Configure AWS OIDC Provider**: Set up GitHub as an OIDC identity provider in AWS IAM
2. **Create IAM Roles**: Create separate IAM roles for dev and prod with OIDC trust policies
3. **Create GitHub Environments**: Set up dev and prod environments in repository settings
4. **Configure Environment Variables**: Add AWS IAM role, ECR, EKS, OpenSearch, and domain configuration per environment
5. **Add Optional Secrets**: Configure SMTP authentication and RAG API key if needed
6. **Set Repository Variables**: Configure global notification and SMTP settings
7. **Deploy RAG Infrastructure**: Use Terragrunt to deploy OpenSearch, security groups, and IRSA (required for RAG service)
8. **Deploy RAG Service**: Deploy RAG service first to create authoritative shared Ingress
9. **Test MkDocs Deployment**: Run manual workflow to validate MkDocs configuration and intelligent indexing
10. **Verify Integration**: Confirm RAG indexing works via `/api/rag/v1/index` endpoint

Detailed configuration instructions are available in the [workflows documentation](workflows/README.md).

[.github/README.md#support--troubleshooting]

## Support & Troubleshooting

For specific issues:

- **EKS Deployment Problems**: Check GitHub Actions logs and verify environment variables are correctly configured
- **OIDC Authentication Issues**: Verify IAM role trust policy allows GitHub Actions from your repository and `id-token: write` permission is set
- **Environment Configuration**: Ensure GitHub environments (dev/prod) are properly set up with required variables
- **Container Build Issues**: Verify ECR repository access and Docker build process in workflow logs
- **Ingress/Domain Issues**: Check NGINX Ingress Controller configuration and DNS settings
- **RAG Service Issues**: Verify OpenSearch cluster is accessible and Bedrock models are available in the region
- **Intelligent Indexing Issues**:
    - Check Kubernetes Job logs: `kubectl logs job/identify-files-job-{sha} -n eapref-app`
    - Verify IRSA service account has OpenSearch permissions
    - Ensure VPC endpoints are configured for OpenSearch access
- **File Filtering Inaccuracies**: Review debug output in job logs showing sitemap paths vs OpenSearch paths
- **Content Indexing Problems**: Check RAG service logs for embedding generation and OpenSearch connectivity
- **Shared Ingress Issues**: Verify RAG service created Ingress with all routing rules (`/api/v1/*` → RAG, `/` → MkDocs)
- **Script Errors**: See [scripts documentation](scripts/README.md#troubleshooting) for content analysis and notification issues
- **Template Issues**: See [templates documentation](templates/README.md#customization) for email template customization
- **AWS EKS Issues**: Check deployment logs in GitHub Actions and EKS cluster events using kubectl
page_texts.25:
[.github/README.md#common-solutions]

### Common Solutions

- **Environment Variable Errors**: Verify variables are set in the correct environment (dev vs prod), not globally
- **OIDC Authentication Errors**: Ensure IAM role ARN is correct and trust policy matches repository
- **ECR Push Failures**: Ensure IAM role has ECR repository permissions for the target environment
- **Ingress Not Working**: Verify NGINX Ingress Controller is installed and shared Ingress resource exists
- **Namespace Issues**: Check if `eapref-app` namespace exists and has proper resource quotas
- **RAG Service 404 Errors**: Verify shared Ingress is routing `/api/v1/*` paths to the RAG service
- **OpenSearch Connection Issues**: Ensure IRSA is configured and service account has proper IAM permissions
- **Kubernetes Job Failures**: Check job logs for OpenSearch connectivity, IRSA permissions, or sitemap parsing errors

**EAP Core Support**: [EAP-Core@mygainwell.onmicrosoft.com](mailto:EAP-Core@mygainwell.onmicrosoft.com?subject=EKS%20Deployment%20Support)
